sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 121.4 ± 17.4 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Rho-tagged OR10H1 was expressed in HEK293 cells and used in a deorphanization screen; surface expression was confirmed via the rho tag and functional ligand-response assays were performed to identify cognate odorants.
sites.rationale: OR10H1 is a class A GPCR (olfactory receptor) with no cleavable signal peptide; TM1 spans residues 25–49 and the N-terminus (residues 1–24) is extracellular. An 'N-terminal' tag on this protein can only land before residue 1 (insert_after_residue = 0), the sole extracellular terminus, giving residue_after = M (seq[0]). The junction is 24 residues from TM1, well above the ≥3-residue minimum. The position is topology_derived because the paper names no residue but exactly one extracellular terminus exists. L2 (same paper, same construct) corroborates L1. PMC5964926 reports full-length OR10H1 expressed as a fusion protein with an N-terminal rhodopsin (rho) tag in a pCI mammalian expression vector, constructed by standard PCR. The construct is membrane-anchored (full-length GPCR). No specific residue number is named for the junction.

sources.claim: This plasmid expressed OR10H1 as a fusion protein with an N-terminal rhodopsin tag.

literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1 and L2) derive from the same publication (PMC5964926) and describe the identical rho-tagged OR10H1 construct; L1 is used as the primary clip. No residue number is stated in either clip, so the position is topology_derived from the single extracellular N-terminus. No internal loop insertions are reported in the ledger for OR10H1 or any close ortholog, so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminus (residues 292–318) is intracellular and therefore not eligible for a surface tag.
